key_insight: A learned convolution-based flux closure can predict atmospheric boundary layer heat and momentum transport more accurately than a standard K-profile scheme while remaining physically interpretable.
engineering_relevance: This offers a practical path to improve coarse-resolution weather, climate, and engineering models by capturing both local and nonlocal turbulent transport across stable and unstable boundary layers.
method: Train a linearized convolution operator on LES-derived nondimensional mean profiles.
Test several first-order closure variants using temperature and velocity inputs to predict heat and momentum fluxes.
Select the best model by minimizing mean squared error on both training and unseen cases, then verify stability in single-column simulations.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports evaluation on high-resolution LES across multiple stability regimes, with performance compared against a standard K-profile closure and validated a posteriori in single-column runs.
watch_item: Performance is demonstrated on idealized homogeneous-surface LES, so transferability to complex terrain, heterogeneity, and real-world atmospheric forcing still needs careful validation.
paper_title: Data-Driven Flux Parameterization for the Atmospheric Boundary Layer
